title: The numbers gate was auditing LESS as the paper got better cross-referenced. Fixed at source.
found_by: a subagent doing the \ref fix; MAIN then verified the mechanism at source and measured the exposure

the_defect.where: .claude/skills/autonomous-paper-agent/scripts/check_numbers.py, SKIP_LINE_PAT defined at line 60 and applied as a WHOLE-LINE skip at line 173
the_defect.mechanism: the pattern matches \ref, \cite, \label, \input and typographic macros. When it matched, the ENTIRE physical line was skipped. So any real numeric claim sharing a line with a cross-reference silently left the audit.
the_defect.why_it_is_worse_than_a_missing_check: the gate still printed numbers_gate_pass: true. It got QUIETER as the manuscript got better cross-referenced -- the pass is what one acts on, so a shrinking denominator reads as success.

the_fix.approach: stop skipping the line; strip only the ARGUMENTS of structural/typographic macros plus bare LaTeX lengths (pt/ex/em/\linewidth...), then audit the rest of the line
the_fix.new_code: MACRO_ARG_PAT + LENGTH_PAT + strip_macro_args(); SKIP_LINE_PAT retained but no longer used as a whole-line veto
the_fix.selftest: 6 hand cases, all PASS: keeps 0.6217/0.50 next to a \ref; keeps 623/12032 next to a \citep; drops 0.05/0.37 from a tabular preamble; drops 3.5 from tabcolsep; does not mistake a citation year 2024/2026 for a claim

result_on_paperC.verdict: the gate got STRICTER by 41 numerals and the paper STILL passes at --max-unmatched 0. Every previously-hidden load-bearing numeral traces to evidence.

failure_class: same family as today's other four: a measurement instrument that moves for a reason unrelated to what it is supposed to measure. Here the instrument's COVERAGE shrank silently as an unrelated property (cross-referencing) improved.
generalisable_rule: a gate must report its own denominator, and a change in that denominator must be surfaced. 'PASS' without 'n audited' cannot distinguish a clean paper from a quiet checker.

second_defect_reported_by_the_agent_NOT_.where: paper_build.py, subprocess.run(..., text=True) at ~line 240 decodes as strict UTF-8
second_defect_reported_by_the_agent_NOT_.symptom: pdfTeX writes the TS1 section glyph to main.log as raw latin-1 0xa7, so a \S anywhere in the document raises UnicodeDecodeError and CRASHES THE BUILD GATE -- not the document, which compiles fine
second_defect_reported_by_the_agent_NOT_.status: OPEN. The agent worked around it by writing 'Section' instead of \S. Fix is errors='replace' on the decode. Any future \S, \pounds, or other TS1 glyph will crash the gate again.
second_defect_reported_by_the_agent_NOT_.MAIN_verified: text=True confirmed at source; the raw-byte claim is the agent's and is plausible but I did not reproduce the crash
